podcast.body: This song is based on the bizarre October 1986 assault on CBS News Anchor Dan Rather in New York City. Rather was attacked by two well-dressed men who repeatedly asked, "Kenneth, what's the frequency?" while punching and kicking him. The attackers were never caught, and their motive remained a mystery, though theories later emerged linking it to a mentally ill man, William Tanger, who believed media personalities like Rather were beaming signals into his head. Another theory connected the phrase to fictional stories by Texas writer Donald Bartholome, who featured a character named Kenneth and the exact phrase, as well as a newsman named Mr. Lather, potentially stemming from a lingering grudge from the late 50s/early 60s when Rather and Bartholome both worked in Texas journalism. "All of which shall culminate in one of REM's best known songs."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
